title: The Display Unit's screen and its bridge
ask: Which display does the Display Unit get, now that no store sells the 900 to 1000 nit bar and no ready-made HDMI bridge exists?
why: You ruled a 900 to 1000 nit bar display through an HDMI bridge (D-269). Looking for it to buy tonight, no store had that display: Waveshare's 12.3inch HDMI LCD is 600 nit, its 12.3inch 1920x720 LCD is 300 nit, and the brightest found, the HannStar HSD123KPW2-D10 panel sold in VSDISPLAY kits, is listed at 850 nit. And no ready-made bridge board was found: the BT817 board gives parallel RGB on a 50-pin flat cable (or LVDS on a 40-pin one, up to 1280 x 800), and nothing sold takes that and gives HDMI - the TFP410 is a chip, so the bridge is a small board to draw and order. The answer decides what the DU's screen is and when the display chain can be lit on the bench. Everything else for the DU and the CU is in tonight's carts.
options:
(a) The 850 nit HannStar panel with an HDMI driver board, and I draw the bridge board (TFP410, the BT817 board's 50-pin cable in, HDMI out) to order with the next boards. About 110 to 250 USD for the panel kit by the listings seen, the bridge a few dollars of board and parts. 50 to 150 nit under your ruling. Nothing arrives tonight; the display chain is lit when the bridge board is back.
(b) The 600 nit Waveshare 12.3inch HDMI LCD, 169.99 USD, in the box with its driver board, cables and a 12 V supply, and I draw the same bridge board. It can be ordered tonight. It is the brightness you ruled out for sun on the dash.
(c) Keep 900 to 1000 nit and I keep looking (industrial and automotive panel sellers, by quote). Nothing is bought for the display now; the DU is built and run without its screen until one is found.
(d) Drop the HDMI bridge and scaler: a panel the BT817 board drives directly on its LVDS connector, at most 1280 x 800. No bridge to draw, but not the 1920 x 720 bar you ruled, and the pages are redrawn to it.
recommend: (a), unless 850 nit is not bright enough for you - then (c)
stops: ordering P118 and P119, ticking Y16, and F3's display bring-up (the DU's boards, radio and firmware go ahead without it)
